correctness.rationale: Conditioning on X_(k)=x splits the remaining sample into independent lower Uniform(0,x) and upper Uniform(x,1) groups. Their exact first two raw-sum moments give a quadratic conditional mean of S^2. Integrating x times that quadratic against the first three beta moments yields the displayed covariance. The marginal variances are standard beta and sample-variance formulas and independently reproduce the correlation. Exact Dirichlet-spacing expansion through n=12 and conditional-beta replay through n=1000 agree with every formula and boundary sign.

value.rationale: Order statistics and sample variance are canonical location/rank and dispersion summaries computed from the same sample. The theorem supplies the entire finite dependence profile rather than one isolated moment: a sharp sign transition at the median, reflection symmetry, and a nondegenerate bulk correlation curve with an explicit maximum. This identifies which sample ranks are most coupled to dispersion and quantifies that coupling at finite n and in the quantile-scale limit.
